title: Event-Driven Architecture
description: Combine SQS and SNS for decoupled, scalable communication in ASP.NET Core.

data.text: Event-driven architecture lets services communicate asynchronously. SNS delivers events, and SQS buffers them so consumers can process at their own pace.

data.title: Fan out events to multiple SQS queues
data.content: Combine SNS topic subscriptions with SQS for parallel processing.

data.title: Move failed messages to a DLQ
data.content: Configure a redrive policy so messages that exceed maxReceiveCount go to a dead-letter queue.

data.title: When to Use SNS vs SQS
data.text: Use SNS when you need to push the same event to multiple destinations. Use SQS when consumers need to pull work at their own pace. Together they give you both broadcast and buffering.

cards.title: SQS
cards.description: Managed message queue for point-to-point communication.

cards.title: SNS
cons: No built-in retry for all protocols

data.title: Design an order processing pipeline
data.description: Use SNS and SQS to decouple order creation from fulfillment.
steps: Create an SNS topic for order events
Create SQS queues for billing, shipping, and analytics
Subscribe each queue to the topic with a filter policy
Publish a test order event and verify it reaches all three queues
data.expectedOutcome: A single order event fans out to three independent workers without blocking the API.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: SNS + SQS provides a robust event-driven foundation
Fan-out lets one event trigger multiple workflows
DLQs isolate poison messages for later investigation
Filter policies reduce unnecessary work for downstream services
data.takeaway: Combining SNS and SQS gives you broadcast, buffering, and reliability in one AWS-native pattern.
